title.sl: Deležniški stavki: walking up, built in 1800
title.it: Le frasi participiali: walking up, built in 1800
title.en: Participle clauses: walking up, built in 1800

rule.sl:
Dva stavka z istim osebkom skrajšaš z **-ing**: **Walking up the fell, I saw a raven.** To je **While I was walking**. Tudi razlog, z **not** naprej: **Not knowing the way, we asked at the inn.** Lahko z malo besedo: **After eating, we went home.** **While waiting, I read the paper.**

Za samostalnikom **-ing** nadomesti who ali which z glagolom: **The man standing by the gate is Jack.** Na severu rečejo tudi *the man stood by the gate*; pisno je **standing**.

Deležnik pomeni, da je bilo narejeno: **a mill built in 1800** (which was built). Tudi na začetku: **Built in 1800, the mill is still there.** **Seen from the tarn, the fell looks small.**

**Having** + deležnik: najprej eno, potem drugo: **Having finished the hay, we went to the inn.** V govoru **After finishing the hay**.

Obe polovici imata isti osebek: **Walking up the fell, I saw a raven.** V *Walking up the fell, a raven flew over me* hodi krokar; ljudje to rečejo in se razume, v skrbnem pisanju pa je **As I was walking up the fell, a raven flew over me.**
rule.de:
Zwei Sätze mit demselben Subjekt kürzt du mit **-ing**: **Walking up the fell, I saw a raven.** Das ist **While I was walking**. Auch ein Grund, mit **not** vorn: **Not knowing the way, we asked at the inn.** Auch mit kleinem Wort: **After eating, we went home.** **While waiting, I read the paper.**

Nach einem Nomen ersetzt **-ing** who oder which mit dem Verb: **The man standing by the gate is Jack.** Im Norden sagt man auch *the man stood by the gate*; geschrieben steht **standing**.

Das Partizip heißt: Es wurde gemacht: **a mill built in 1800** (which was built). Auch am Anfang: **Built in 1800, the mill is still there.** **Seen from the tarn, the fell looks small.**

**Having** + Partizip: zuerst das eine, dann das andere: **Having finished the hay, we went to the inn.** Gesprochen **After finishing the hay**.

Beide Hälften haben dasselbe Subjekt: **Walking up the fell, I saw a raven.** In *Walking up the fell, a raven flew over me* geht der Rabe; man sagt das und versteht es, aber sorgfältig geschrieben steht **As I was walking up the fell, a raven flew over me.**
rule.it:
Due frasi con lo stesso soggetto si accorciano con **-ing**, come il gerundio: **Walking up the fell, I saw a raven.** È **While I was walking**. Anche un motivo, con **not** davanti: **Not knowing the way, we asked at the inn.** Anche con una parolina: **After eating, we went home.** **While waiting, I read the paper.**

Dopo un nome **-ing** sostituisce who o which col verbo: **The man standing by the gate is Jack.** Al nord si dice anche *the man stood by the gate*; per iscritto si usa **standing**.

Il participio dice che è stato fatto: **a mill built in 1800** (which was built). Anche all'inizio: **Built in 1800, the mill is still there.** **Seen from the tarn, the fell looks small.**

**Having** + participio: prima una cosa, poi l'altra: **Having finished the hay, we went to the inn.** A voce **After finishing the hay**.

Le due metà hanno lo stesso soggetto: **Walking up the fell, I saw a raven.** In *Walking up the fell, a raven flew over me* cammina il corvo; si dice e si capisce, ma nello scritto curato si usa **As I was walking up the fell, a raven flew over me.**
rule.en:
Two clauses with one subject get shorter with **-ing**: **Walking up the fell, I saw a raven.** That's **While I was walking**. A reason too, with **not** first: **Not knowing the way, we asked at the inn.** A small word can come first: **After eating, we went home.** **While waiting, I read the paper.**

After a noun **-ing** takes the place of who or which and the verb: **The man standing by the gate is Jack.** In the North people also say *the man stood by the gate*; writing wants **standing**.

The participle says it was done: **a mill built in 1800** (which was built). At the start too: **Built in 1800, the mill is still there.** **Seen from the tarn, the fell looks small.**

**Having** + the participle: one thing first, then the other: **Having finished the hay, we went to the inn.** In talk **After finishing the hay**.

Both halves have one subject: **Walking up the fell, I saw a raven.** In *Walking up the fell, a raven flew over me* the raven walks; people say it and you understand them, but careful writing wants **As I was walking up the fell, a raven flew over me.**
